question: Are flower-colour profiles of sympatric plant species more similar or more divergent than independently matched allopatric controls, and which ecological contexts predict the sign?

relationship_to_G1_G4.distinction: G1-G4 concern within-species colour geography; G5 concerns between-species community assembly and sympatry.

sympatry_frame.source: independent frozen GBIF vascular-plant occurrence download, excluding the iNaturalist flower-photo records used for colour measurement where identifiers can be matched
sympatry_frame.allopatric_candidate: zero overlap after one-cell dilation of both species occupancy masks
sympatry_frame.claim_boundary: This primary frame establishes geographic sympatry, not direct ecological interaction. The term co-flowering is reserved for the secondary phenology-qualified subset.

outcome_blind_matching.unit: one focal species x one sympatric partner
exact_match: taxonomic distance class relative to focal: congeneric / same-family noncongeneric / different-family
nearest_match_covariates: four-axis CHELSA climate-centroid difference from focal using BIO1/BIO4/BIO12/BIO15 standardized without colour
outcome_blind_matching.selection_rule: choose up to five allopatric controls with smallest Euclidean distance in the standardized matching covariates, deterministic hash tie-break; discard the matched set unless at least two controls have matching distance <= 1.5

colour_distance.primary: Jensen-Shannon distance between species mean soft four-group flower-colour palette vectors within each frozen 20-photo Monte Carlo draw
colour_distance.sensitivity: distance between location-blind CIELAB species centroids; never substitute for the primary result

primary_statistic.matched_set_delta: D_colour(sympatric partner) - mean D_colour(matched allopatric controls)
primary_statistic.focal_weighting: average matched-set deltas within focal species, then equal-weight focal species
primary_statistic.primary_test: two-sided deviation from matched allopatric expectation

null.scheme: within each frozen matched set, randomly choose one partner from the observed sympatric partner plus its matched allopatric controls as pseudo-sympatric and treat the remaining partners as pseudo-controls

species_characterization.score: equal-set mean delta for each focal species
species_characterization.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across evaluable focal species
species_characterization.claim_boundary: Species labels are descriptive community-embedding profiles, not causal evolutionary diagnoses.

predeclared_context_tests.prediction_competing: high shared pollinator-guild overlap can produce either convergence through shared signalling/filtering or divergence through partitioning; sign is estimated rather than selected
predeclared_context_tests.source: frozen GBIF pollinator-guild and GloBI layers from G3
predeclared_context_tests.stratification: external-data-only median split before colour inference

predeclared_context_tests.prediction: sympatric divergence should be strongest for congeners, especially when flowering overlap is high
predeclared_context_tests.phenology_requirement: secondary only when independent metadata support at least two overlapping flowering months for both species

predeclared_context_tests.prediction: sympatric convergence may be strongest among noncongeneric species sharing similar pollinator guilds
sympatric convergence may track strong environmental similarity even after taxonomic matching

coflowering_secondary_subset.definition: geographically sympatric pair plus at least two overlapping flowering months from outcome-blind phenology metadata

claim_ceiling: A supported G5 result establishes non-random flower-colour similarity or divergence among geographically sympatric species relative to outcome-blind matched allopatric controls. It does not by itself establish facilitation, competition, reproductive interference, mimicry or pollinator-mediated character displacement.
